subject: CloudRetail POC: routing policy workshop & load test scheduling
messages:
From: Mike Chen <mike.chen@cloudretail.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 09 Jan 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: POC kickoff: scheduling and scope questions

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to move to a short PoC to validate routing-based cost reductions and fallback behavior under load. Would you be able to run a hands-on workshop with our infra + product folks next week? We were thinking 60–90 minutes to cover: prompt review, model selection, routing tiers, and at least a light load test.

Tentative windows that work for us:
- Tue 2027-01-12 (late afternoon ET)
- Wed 2027-01-13 (anytime ET)
- Thu 2027-01-14 (morning ET)

Attaching a one-page overview of the goals. Also, can you confirm what model variants (FP16 / int8) you recommend we have ready and whether a low-latency fallback to a smaller model is supported?

Mike Chen
Product Lead, CloudRetail
mike.chen@cloudretail.com
Phone: +1 415-555-0199

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mike Chen <mike.chen@cloudretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC kickoff: scheduling and scope questions

Mike — thanks for the clear goals, this is exactly the right scope. Quick answers up front: yes, we can cover model variants (we typically bring both a FP16 candidate and an int8-quantized variant for cost comparisons) and we support an automatic fallback path to a smaller model instance group in the routing policy.

Availability: I have a calendar conflict on 1/12 afternoon but can do either 2027-01-13 or 2027-01-18. Ben and Lauren are looped in to help run the load test and the routing policy workshop respectively. Connor will take notes / own the runbook write-up.

Proposed plan (draft agenda attached):
- 15m: goals, success metrics, and prompt samples (CloudRetail)
- 30–40m: routing policy + model variants (Redwood walkthrough + Q&A)
- 20–30m: live load test (throughput/latency checks, KV cache checks)
- 10m: next steps & rollout plan

If 1/13 is good for you, what time window (EST) do you prefer? If not, we can move to 1/18 (we'll need the full 90m).

Calendly to propose times: https://calendly.com/redwood/poc-hands-on-45m

Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 08:43:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: CloudRetail PoC - prep checklist and role assignments

Team — internal prep to make 1/13 (3:30pm ET) a smooth hands-on session. Mike confirmed 1/13 at 15:30 ET; I accepted the slot and sent a tentative invite. Key asks: 

- Ben: please bring the quantized int8 candidate and be prepared to run the throughput comparison. Output we need: token/sec and cost-per-token delta vs FP16 for 30/60/120 context lengths.
- Lauren: lead routing policy design (tiering + fallback rules). Have a short slide on recommended defaults for e-comm traffic patterns.
- Connor: own the runbook and capture all test outputs in the shared drive.

Prep checklist (short):
- confirm test harness (k6 script) and attach load_test_template.csv to the runbook
- prepare prompt samples (Mike shared initial set) — we'll pare to 8 canonical prompts
- spin up model variants in staging (FP16 + int8), ensure KV cache warm path is enabled
- create a fallback policy demo (tier small-model / cheap-model) with automatic routing switch on latency > 300ms

I'll draft the routing policy checklist and upload it to the Drive link below. If anybody can't make 1/13 at 3:30pm ET ping me immediately — otherwise we'll assume the slot is firm.

Karthik

Related link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bPoC-CloudRetail
